newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: European bunkers end week with further losses.
newsitem.headline: European bunkers end week with further losses.

text.p: European bunkers slipped once again on Friday, although the falls were minor compared to the average daily loss this week, dealers said.
In northern Europe, demand remained thin, but buyers in the Mediterranean were drawn back in. Traders said a number in southern Europe now felt the market had bottomed out.
Rotterdam 380 CST fuel oil was trading, albeit thinly, in a range of $106/$107 fob, down about $2 on the day by late afternoon. Bunkers were thus at their lowest levels since the very end of August.
Hamburg prices also headed down, by around $1/$2 to $117/$118 fob. Traders said demand was slow to normal.
Bunkers at most Mediterranean ports were down by around $2 a tonne. Unlike in the north, prices were not at exceptional lows, having reached below such levels in December.
Demand picked up in Spain, Italy and France.
Further east, Egyptian prices were down by around $3 a tonne. Supplies in Alexandria were rather tight.
Fujairah bunkers dropped by about $2, but just held above the $100 mark.
